title: Every Site in the House
tagline: Every site on my network, listed, and nobody has to keep the list.
what: A page that lists every web app on my home network: what runs it, whether it is up, and how new it is. It rebuilds itself every minute from the network's own settings, so there is no list to keep up.
built: Made the page build its list from the web server's own settings and what is running on the box
New sites appear on their own, removed ones stay listed for 90 days, and a moved site's port follows it
Kept the last good list when a source fails, and put the failure on the page instead of turning it all red
Added a crash alert and a stale-page banner if the rebuild stops
credit: I built the page and the automatic site finder

making.problem: I could not always find the sites on my own network, tell what they were, or see whether they were running.
how: Every minute a small program reads the web server's own settings and checks what is running behind each site.
It adds each page's own title and the earliest sign it existed, and checks whether it answers.
Anything it cannot read is said on the page. If a whole run crashes, the page keeps the last good list and shows a banner.
credits: Caddy: web server; Docker: app runner
systemd: service manager; Pi-hole: network names

log.text: Built the page and its one-minute agent, and put it live.
Forced a crash in a test copy: the page kept its last good list and showed the crash banner.

serviceRecord.purpose: Every site in the house, what runs it and whether it is up, with no list to keep.

receipt.title: The last good list stays.
receipt.text: I forced a test copy to stop rebuilding. The page kept the last good list and showed a warning, so I could still find the sites while seeing that the list needed attention.

serviceRecord.care: Never add a site by hand. Fix where it comes from and the list follows.

entries.text: Built it and put it live. It rebuilds every minute, in about 3.5 seconds.
Added pages without a name yet and names with no working site behind them.
Tested the crash path in a copy. The banner and the last good list held.

back.pitch: A directory that updates itself. New sites appear within about two minutes, removed ones age out, and the page flags any source it cannot read.
cut: Built from the web server’s own settings and the apps running on the box.
Every site shows what runs it, when it last restarted and when it was added.
